title: Compactness and the Boolean prime ideal principle
summary: Prove over ZF that Boolean prime ideal extension, the ultrafilter extension principle, and arbitrary-atom propositional compactness are equivalent.
abstract: A family of Boolean requirements may be compatible whenever only finitely many are considered. Propositional compactness asks for one truth assignment satisfying them all. Ultrafilter extension asks for a compatible family of large sets to be enlarged until every set or its complement has been chosen. Working over ZF set theory, we prove that these are equivalent to extending proper filters on Boolean algebras, the filter form of the Boolean prime ideal principle. Truth sets of all valuations turn an ultrafilter into a simultaneous solution, while finite Boolean subalgebras make the reverse compactness argument possible. The constructions apply to arbitrary sets of atoms and isolate the extension principle without assuming the full axiom of choice.
